meta.title: MCO · One review, individual provider answers
meta.subtitle: Default CLI / shim path · no chain, debate or synthesis · checked-out revision 3cfce13

components.label: Review CLI
components.explanation: Accepts one CLI request. Resolves configuration and prompt; validates target paths against repository and allow_paths; creates one invocation per selected provider/model (or explicit --agent). Builds the adapter map and checks policy support before starting. Review defaults to read_only, but explicit execution mode and permission overrides can change it; this is not an unconditional MCO sandbox.

components.label: Invocation runtime
components.explanation: run_invocation_workflow delegates directly to run_invocations when chain, debate and synthesis are off. A worker per invocation builds TaskInput with prompt, repo, scope, model and permissions. The pool is bounded by max_provider_parallelism when positive, otherwise by invocation count. Workers start adapters, poll status and read raw stdout logs, decode provider transport into answer deltas and final text, and enforce stall/hard/global deadlines and cancellation.

components.label: Provider adapters
components.explanation: The registry maps provider IDs to provider-specific adapters, such as ClaudeAdapter and CodexAdapter. In the default shim path, ShimAdapterBase spawns a subprocess in repo_root, captures stdout/stderr in raw log files, and exposes run/poll/cancel. Provider subclasses build commands and decode their wire format; Codex, for example, uses exec --json and maps sandbox/model/prompt options. ACP and configured custom agents are optional alternatives, not shown as mandatory hops.

components.label: Provider CLI processes
components.explanation: Each shim invocation starts the selected provider executable with cwd set to the requested repository. Raw stdout/stderr are redirected to files and consumed through MCO's adapter/runtime path. This source establishes the subprocess boundary, not the provider's internal reasoning, network endpoints, credentials or actual remote execution. Provider binaries were not run for this diagram.

sources.label: Executable, cwd, I/O and PID boundary

components.label: Result collection
components.explanation: A logical responsibility within run_invocations, not a separate service. Futures are consumed as they finish, but results are stored by original invocation index, preserving selection order in outputs[]. Each result carries invocation_id, provider, model, status, output, error and exit_code (plus deltas/transport details when available). Exceptions and cancellation become individual failure results. All success gives complete/0; some success gives partial/1; none gives failed/2. There is no default answer merge or review verdict synthesis.

components.label: CLI response
components.explanation: Another responsibility of runtime/cli.py, not an extra process. Default stdout streams decoded text, adding invocation/provider/model headers when multiple sources alternate. JSONL emits lifecycle and delta events. --json prints a final task envelope containing outputs[] with stderr removed, then returns the aggregate exit code. Diagnostics go to stderr in the non-JSON event path. --result-mode artifact can suppress answer stdout; both retains both outputs.

components.label: Local review artifacts
components.explanation: Filesystem output, not a database server. The runtime writes decoded deltas into stages/run/invocations/<invocation_id>.md. If persistence is requested, InvocationArtifactWriter writes result.md and run.json under artifact_base/task_id, with raw provider runs under provider-runs/. Otherwise all working files use a temporary directory, artifact paths are nulled in returned outputs, and the temporary directory is cleaned up. The collector owns summary writes; the invocation worker owns incremental answer writes.

boundaries.label: MCO Python process · in-process calls, worker threads and callbacks

cards.title: One request, N independent answers
items: Selected providers become provider/model invocations, not separate review requests.
Concurrency is bounded when configured; outputs[] preserves selection order, not finish order.
Failure of one invocation can yield a partial task rather than discard successful answers.

cards.title: Scope and enforcement
items: Default CLI + shim path only; chain, debate, synthesis, ACP and custom-agent variants are not expanded.
Review defaults to read_only; configuration and permission overrides matter. No unconditional sandbox is implied.
Entry, output and collection boxes are logical roles, not separate services.

cards.title: Evidence boundary
items: Source references are attached to each component at pinned revision 3cfce13.
Provider internals and network behavior are outside the checked-out implementation; no remote service is inferred.
Raw log I/O belongs to the adapter/runtime path; stored review outputs are local files, not a database.
